title: eval-harness: add per-prompt quality gating + CI metrics integration
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds CI-driven per-prompt quality gating for eval-harness. CI will fail on regressed prompts based on configurable thresholds; includes docs and rollout plan.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see subtle regressions in model prompt behavior that are not captured by aggregate metrics. This PR adds per-prompt quality gating to the eval-harness and wires the results into CI so that a PR can fail if a configured prompt set falls below a threshold.

What this changes: - eval-harness: emit per-prompt metrics (exact match, BLEU, answer-coverage) in a consistent JSON artifact. - ci/eval-gate.yml: new GitHub Actions job that downloads the eval artifact and applies per-prompt thresholds defined in eval/prompt-thresholds.yaml. The job fails the build when more than N prompts regress by the configured delta. - eval/prompt-thresholds.yaml: canonical thresholds for the core prompt sets used by the platform. Defaults are conservative to avoid noise. - tooling: bin/compare_eval.py (small CLI used by CI to compute deltas and produce a human-readable summary). - docs: docs/eval/ci-gates.md with rollout instructions and troubleshooting.

Testing: - Unit tests for metrics serialization and compare logic. - End-to-end CI job was run on a staging branch and validated with controlled regressions. - Thresholds were tested against the last 6 weeks of CI baselines to estimate expected false-positive rate.

Rollout plan: - Merge as opt-in (new job is added but gated by repo-level boolean in .github/eval-gates-config). After 48h we will enable for the redwood repo. For Dedicated/Private customers the job is informational only unless explicitly enabled.

Notes: This PR keeps the threshold file small and documented. Future work: auto-calibration of thresholds, per-model baseline tracking, and a dashboard that surfaces prompt-level regressions to owners.

review_comments: Ava Thompson: This looks good overall — two concerns: a) thresholds might be too tight for low-sample prompts, b) we need clearer guidance for flakiness reruns. Can you add calibration notes and an option to mark prompts as 'unstable'?
Maya Chen: +1 on adding 'unstable' metadata; added eval/prompt-thresholds.yaml with 'stability' flags and documented rerun guidance in docs/eval/ci-gates.md.

Liam O'Connor: Small nit: prefer a shorter human summary in the GH checks output. Suggest adding a one-line status in bin/compare_eval.py output. Updated in the most recent commit.
Ava Thompson: Approving after the stability and docs updates. Left one comment about logging level in metrics.py (keep at info).
Maya Chen: Addressed logging nits and added unit tests for the compare utility. Thanks!
